decisions.title: Close the Outlook send and reconcile gates
decisions.proposedAction: Close the quote delivery gate (#294) and the Outlook reconciliation gate (#297) on the development commissioning evidence.
decisions.consequence: Both gates close and the Local V1 checklist item for Outlook delivery is met.
decisions.scope: Development only. One non-customer quote, already sent and reconciled once. No new send, no customer recipient, no production.

evidence.label: Commissioning evidence and gaps (ledger comment on #697)

missingPrerequisites: No direct trace shows the immutable-ID header on draft creation (required by #294).
No recorded pending, executing, provider-reference and indeterminate transition history exists for the delivery (required by #294).
No live run shows that parallel workers cannot produce duplicate terminal records (required by #297).
The blocked repeat send is evidenced only by the tool's own assertion, not by the repeat action's recorded status.
decisions.rollback: Reopen #294 and #297. Nothing was changed on the runtime by accepting the evidence.

decisions.title: Authorise the isolated restore and restart proof
decisions.proposedAction: Run capture, isolated restore, reread, rollback and the restart proof against an isolated local backend, and record the evidence.
decisions.consequence: Produces the recovery evidence Local V1 needs. The live data directory is read, never written; the driver refuses any non-loopback or configured target. The evidence directory must exist before the run; the driver never creates it.
decisions.scope: Development only, on the Lenovo host, against a throwaway loopback backend.

evidence.label: Independent review of the merged driver: pass, no findings

decisions.rollback: Delete the isolated backend and its restored copy. Live data is untouched by design.

decisions.title: Authorise a model-provider key for Totality reasoning
decisions.proposedAction: Configure a model-provider API key on the Lenovo development runtime through the approved secret onboarding path.
decisions.consequence: The HUD and API reasoning service stops reporting not-configured and can produce proposal-only reasoning. This starts paid usage on the provider account. It does not change voice: the voice path does not call the model.
decisions.scope: Development runtime only. One secret, stored where the runtime reads its other secrets. Not committed.

evidence.label: Voice commissioning audit: the key is not a voice prerequisite

decisions.rollback: Remove the key from the runtime and revoke it at the provider.

decisions.title: Accept guarded voice commissioning
decisions.proposedAction: Accept the guarded voice interface as commissioned on the Lenovo host.
decisions.consequence: The voice item on the Local V1 checklist is met and #567 can close. Physical machinery control stays out of scope.
decisions.scope: Development host only: microphone, speaker, wake word, confirmations and typed fallback.
missingPrerequisites: Pull request #804 (the HUD shows and speaks the clarification question) is not merged and running on the host.
No microphone and audibility acceptance run has been recorded on the real host.
Ten dispatch round-trip samples from the owner's own HUD session have not been recorded.
decisions.rollback: Reopen #567. Voice can be disabled by leaving the microphone off; no hardware adapter ships.

decisions.title: Authorise one governed Google Home announcement
decisions.proposedAction: Pin one named speaker and play one governed test announcement through the existing ToolAction path.
decisions.consequence: A speaker in the house plays audio once. This commissions the home announcement path for Local V1.
decisions.scope: One pinned Cast device, one announcement, development runtime. The ToolAction approval for the announcement itself is still required separately.
missingPrerequisites: No pinned speaker target has been named; the pinned-target map is absent.
decisions.rollback: Remove the pinned-target map; the announcement path then fails closed again.

decisions.title: tcp-check decision 2: keep the narrow worker egress scope
decisions.proposedAction: Accept the scope stated in the specification: the kernel blocks every process except the broker from reaching any target that is or ever was allowlisted, and the Jarvis service keeps its general outbound access.
decisions.consequence: The Jarvis service can still open connections to unrelated addresses, as it does today for Convex and Microsoft Graph. Rejecting this card means requiring default-deny outbound for the whole service, which is stronger and considerably more work.
decisions.scope: Planning decision only. It changes the specification a builder works from; it authorises no code, no host change and no target.

evidence.label: Independent review of the specification: pass, no findings

decisions.rollback: Record a later decision requiring default-deny outbound; the enforcer specification is then amended before it is built.

decisions.title: tcp-check decision 3: approve a host-local synthetic test target
decisions.proposedAction: Approve using a listener inside a private network namespace on the Lenovo, reached over a virtual link, as the only target for the adversarial test matrix.
decisions.consequence: No test packet leaves the machine and no third-party address is ever contacted. The exact address is chosen so that it is outside the special-use table.
decisions.scope: Planning decision only. It changes the specification a builder works from; it authorises no code, no host change and no target.

evidence.label: Independent review of the specification: pass, no findings

missingPrerequisites: The exact address has not been proposed and reviewed.
decisions.rollback: Withdraw the approval; the evidence run cannot then be prepared.

decisions.title: tcp-check decision 4: confirm 30 seconds as the fail-safe teardown delay
decisions.proposedAction: Confirm T_live at 30 seconds: when the control plane has failed, a live target stays reachable by the broker for at most 30 seconds after its last refresh.
decisions.consequence: A shorter value closes the window sooner and costs more frequent kernel updates; a longer value does the opposite. Thirty seconds is the proposal in the specification.
decisions.scope: Planning decision only. It changes the specification a builder works from; it authorises no code, no host change and no target.

evidence.label: Independent review of the specification: pass, no findings

decisions.rollback: Record a different value; the specification's constants are then amended.

decisions.title: tcp-check decision 5: accept root-owned components on the development host
decisions.proposedAction: Accept that the rule set, the renewer, the resume hook, the lock files and the guard unit run as root on the Lenovo, that the Jarvis service will not start if the guard unit fails (including when the store cannot be reached at boot), and that the control plane may kill a stopped renewer.
decisions.consequence: Jarvis gains root-owned parts and its startup becomes dependent on the firewall rules and the store. A failed rule load stops the whole service rather than leaving former targets reachable.
decisions.scope: Planning decision only. It changes the specification a builder works from; it authorises no code, no host change and no target.

evidence.label: Independent review of the specification: pass, no findings

decisions.rollback: Withdraw the acceptance before anything is installed; after installation, remove the units, the rule set and the broker user.

decisions.title: tcp-check decision 6: keep every single-use ledger row
decisions.proposedAction: Keep every tcp-check ledger row indefinitely. No archive rule.
decisions.consequence: The ledger grows by at most ten rows per owner per minute of use and is never pruned, so a retired claim can never be presented again. An archive rule can be decided later.
decisions.scope: Planning decision only. It changes the specification a builder works from; it authorises no code, no host change and no target.

evidence.label: Independent review of the specification: pass, no findings

decisions.rollback: Define an archive rule later; nothing is deleted in the meantime.

decisions.title: tcp-check decision 7: enforce permission expiry in the kernel (option 7a)
decisions.proposedAction: Choose option 7a: the lease is enforced in the kernel as well as in the store and the broker, so an expired capability is rejected at the connect call itself. Confirm T_call at 1 000 ms.
decisions.consequence: This keeps the scope locked on #779 intact. It requires a further short specification (helper interface, clock mapping, skew allowance) before the time workstream can be built. Rejecting this card and choosing 7b instead means accepting a small gap and formally loosening the locked scope.
decisions.scope: Planning decision only. It changes the specification a builder works from; it authorises no code, no host change and no target.

evidence.label: Independent review of the specification: pass, no findings

decisions.rollback: Record 7b instead; the specification is amended to state the weaker contract.

decisions.title: tcp-check decision 8: accept the bounded clock assumption
decisions.proposedAction: Confirm 5 000 ms as the allowed difference between a component's clock and store time, T_guard at 2 000 ms, and that exact expiry is proved only if the store's clock never steps back unseen by more than T_guard. Confirm that resetting the time high-water mark is an owner-only action.
decisions.consequence: Expiry is checked two seconds early, shortening the usable lease to 13 seconds. A backward clock step larger than two seconds that no write observed is outside what the design can detect. Rejecting this card means requiring a second trusted time source.
decisions.scope: Planning decision only. It changes the specification a builder works from; it authorises no code, no host change and no target.

evidence.label: Independent review of the specification: pass, no findings

decisions.rollback: Record a requirement for a second time source; the time specification is amended before it is built.

decisions.title: Approve building the tcp-check egress enforcer (WS-A)
decisions.proposedAction: Approve implementation of the egress enforcer specification: a separate broker process and a root-owned kernel rule set.
decisions.consequence: Work starts on code that owns a real network socket, behind the default-deny registry entry, to the merged specification (docs/design/issue-779-tcp-check-commissioning-specs.md, WS-A).
decisions.scope: Development only. Draft pull requests; the capability stays planned and no real target is allowlisted.

evidence.label: Independent review of the specification: pass, no findings

decisions.rollback: Close the implementation pull requests; remove the rule set and broker user from the host.

decisions.title: Approve building the tcp-check durable store (WS-B)
decisions.proposedAction: Approve implementation of the durable single-use store specification.
decisions.consequence: Work starts on the store transactions that grant the sole right to connect and record outcomes.
decisions.scope: Development only. Draft pull requests; no socket is opened by this workstream.

evidence.label: Independent review of the specification: pass, no findings

decisions.rollback: Close the implementation pull requests.

decisions.title: Approve building the tcp-check time rules (WS-C)
decisions.proposedAction: Approve implementation of the clock, deadline, rate-window and port-range specification.
decisions.consequence: Work starts on the trusted-clock checks and the rule for recording a timeout versus an unknown effect.
decisions.scope: Development only. Draft pull requests.

evidence.label: Independent review of the specification: pass, no findings

missingPrerequisites: If decision 7 chooses option 7a, the kernel-lease mechanism needs its own reviewed specification before this workstream is built.
decisions.rollback: Close the implementation pull requests.

decisions.title: Authorise the tcp-check adversarial evidence run (WS-D)
decisions.proposedAction: Run the 22-case adversarial matrix against a host-local synthetic target.
decisions.consequence: Real TCP connections are attempted on the development host, to a listener that never leaves the machine.
decisions.scope: Development host only. One synthetic, host-local target approved for this run. No third-party target.
missingPrerequisites: The enforcer, store and time workstreams are not implemented.
No synthetic test target has been chosen.
decisions.rollback: Stop the broker, flush the kernel rule set and remove the test network namespace.

decisions.title: Promote tcp-check and allow the first development target (WS-E)
decisions.proposedAction: Move the tcp-check capability out of planned, populate the reviewed allowlist and allow the first authorised development target.
decisions.consequence: Jarvis can make governed TCP connection checks to the allowlisted target. Each check still needs its own T3 approval.
decisions.scope: Development only. One reviewed allowlist entry.
missingPrerequisites: No passing adversarial evidence run exists.
decisions.rollback: Empty the allowlist and set the registry entry back to planned; the capability is default-deny again.

decisions.title: Release Jarvis Local V1
decisions.proposedAction: Declare one exact release candidate as Jarvis Local V1.
decisions.consequence: Jarvis becomes the daily system for business, home and workshop on the local runtime.
decisions.scope: The local runtime on the Lenovo host. No remote exposure, no production deployment, no physical machinery control.
missingPrerequisites: No release candidate commit has been frozen.
The complete Beez Treez workflow has not been proven end to end.
No integrated dogfood pass has been recorded.
No independent review of a release candidate exists.
The operator runbook and release evidence are not recorded.
decisions.rollback: Return to the previous known-good commit and restore from the recovery archive.

decisions.title: Commission remote access
decisions.proposedAction: Expose Jarvis beyond the local machine behind the chosen identity provider and TLS terminator.
decisions.consequence: Jarvis becomes reachable from outside the host. A mistake here exposes business and home data.
decisions.scope: One public hostname, one identity provider, one exact release.
missingPrerequisites: No identity provider has been chosen.
No public hostname or TLS terminator has been chosen.
No live authentication, proxy-spoofing, origin or rate-limit evidence exists.
No exact release has been proposed.
decisions.rollback: Rebind to loopback and disable the remote gateway; revoke the application registration.

decisions.title: Approve a production runtime
decisions.proposedAction: Deploy one exact release to an authorised hosted production runtime.
decisions.consequence: Jarvis runs in production with real data. Requires backup, restore, secret rotation, restart, rollback and alerting to be proven first.
decisions.scope: One hosted runtime and its production database.
missingPrerequisites: No production host or runtime has been chosen.
No telemetry and retention policy has been decided.
No backup and restore, secret rotation, restart, rollback or alerting drill evidence exists.
No exact release has been proposed.
decisions.rollback: Roll back to the recorded previous release and restore from the proven backup.

decisions.title: Commission live durable orchestration
decisions.proposedAction: Wire the durable orchestration boundary into live trigger paths on the commissioned runtime.
decisions.consequence: Scheduled and triggered work can run unattended against real providers.
decisions.scope: The commissioned runtime only, after one bounded commissioning exercise.
missingPrerequisites: No commissioned runtime, remote identity or gateway exists.
No restart, lease recovery, duplicate-trigger or provider reconciliation evidence exists on a deployment.
decisions.rollback: Disconnect the trigger ingress; the offline composition remains inert.
